title: Graceful quarantine + resume for stalled on-prem tenant upgrades caused by intermittent Helm hook failures
creator: Connor Liu
description:
Summary:
Several on-prem customers escalated when tenant upgrades would hang in 'Installing' or 'Finalizing' for >30 minutes. Root cause investigations across incidents showed intermittent Helm hook failures (post-install/post-upgrade) where hooks that create transient jobs or secrets sometimes failed due to API throttling or a race with finalizers. The operator kept the tenant in a partially upgraded state and normal reconciliation would retry forever, blocking traffic and tenant rollforward.

Goal:
Provide an automated, safe quarantine mechanism and resume flow so: 1) stuck tenant upgrades are isolated from the global upgrade controller; 2) any partial state (helm release, jobs, secrets, finalizers) is recorded and checkpointed; 3) operator can surface a clear remediation for SREs & customers and optionally resume the upgrade after automated remediation or manual confirmation.

Background & constraints:
- Must not risk data loss for tenant KV stores or permanent downgrade of tenant CRs.
- Quarantine should be reversible and observable (events, audit log entries).
- Avoid large blast radius; default to quarantining only the single tenant namespace and its helm release.
- Should work for VPC/on-prem installs where cluster-level permissions are limited.

Acceptance criteria:
- Operator detects Helm hook failure patterns and automatically transitions tenant CR to a new state 'upgrade-quarantined' with a human-readable reason and timestamp.
- Quarantined tenants are excluded from global upgrade waves and do not block other tenants in same controller batch.
- A 'repair' subcommand (operator CLI and web-console button) runs idempotent remediation steps (recreate missing job, remove stuck finalizers, reconcile helm hooks) and either resumes the upgrade or marks for manual intervention.
- Telemetry: alert rule and dashboard panels to show number and age of quarantine events, top failure reasons, and per-customer TTL to force manual intervention after configurable time.

Proposed solution (high-level):
1) Detection: augment Helm watcher with heuristics: consecutive hook failures >=2 within 10m OR helm release state 'pending-upgrade' with resource jobs stuck + pod crashloop. Emit event and annotate tenant CR.
2) Quarantine: set tenant annotation 'inference.redwood/upgrade-quarantined: true' and create a small configmap 'quarantine-metadata' with helm release name, last-hook-logs (first 32KB) and kube objects snapshot (list of API resources). Do not delete resources automatically.
3) Isolation: operator will exclude annotated tenants from batch upgrade waves and autoscaling operations, mark them on console with a bright warning, and notify on-call via existing PagerDuty routing for customer-impacting quarantines.
4) Repair flow: implement a repair job run by operator (RBAC-permission-limited) that attempts safe operations in order: a) remove obvious stuck finalizers (if owned by operator-managed controllers), b) recreate missing hook jobs from cached templates, c) re-run helm upgrade with --force --recreate-pods to reconcile. Each operation is logged and checkpointed. The repair job is guarded by a dry-run first and a per-tenant rate limit.
5) Resume/rollback: after successful repair, remove quarantine annotation and emit an event 'upgrade-resumed'. If repair fails after N attempts (configurable), mark tenant 'upgrade-failed' and write a runbook pointer to tenant status with next steps and TEAMS/Slack escalation.

Runbook & customer comms:
- Confluence runbook created: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Quarantine+for+Stalled+Upgrades (link placeholder).
- Incident template added to Oncall playbooks with suggested message to send to customers, including the 'quarantine id' and how to request manual rollback.

Testing plan:
- Unit tests for detector heuristics and annotation transitions.
- Integration tests on kind/k3d with injected helm hook failures (simulate API throttling, job crash).
- Staging canary: enable quarantine on 5% of tenant waves in staging clusters and validate that other tenants are unaffected.
- Post-merge smoke: run repair flow on a synthetic tenant and assert 'upgrade-resumed' event and no data loss.

Rollout strategy:
- Phase 1: operator binary with detection + annotation only (no auto-repair), rollout to staging clusters and 20% of onprem customers (config flag).
- Phase 2: enable automated repair with strict dry-run logging for 24h, behind feature flag per-tenant.
- Phase 3: full enablement + console UI for manual 'Repair' button.

Related risks and mitigations:
- Accidentally removing customer-owned finalizers: only remove finalizers that match operator-owned patterns; require manual override for unknown finalizers.
- Insufficient RBAC to run repair operations: provide a fallback user-visible remediation checklist and a one-off escalation path for customer SRE.

updates: 2026-01-14 - Connor Liu opened ticket after postmortem for two customer incidents where helm hook jobs were OOMKilled and left releases in pending state.

2026-01-15 - Initial triage: reproduced hook failure locally by injecting job crash. Determined detection heuristics and quarantine annotation design. Discussed trade-offs with Platform Security (do not delete secrets).

2026-01-16 - Design review with Eng + PM + SRE. Agreed Phase 1 detection-only rollout. Requested follow-up: add console messaging and PagerDuty policy mapping. Assigned to Marta Kovacs for implementation.

2026-01-18 - Spike completed: operator can now annotate tenant CR and write quarantine-metadata configmap. Created draft Confluence runbook. Added tests to operator-e2e harness. PR 4892 created (WIP).
2026-01-20 - Customer A notified about quarantine feature pilot. They granted permission to enable detection-only mode in their staging cluster. Monitoring query added to staging dashboard.
2026-01-22 - Began coding repair job. Found a permission gap for removing finalizers in some customer clusters; opened ENG-743211 to track RBAC minimums.
steps_to_reproduce: Install sample tenant helm chart with a post-install hook that creates a Job which exits non-zero intermittently
Simulate API throttling by applying resource-intensive operations timed with hook execution
Observe tenant CR stuck in 'Installing' and operator emitting repeated reconcile attempts
proposed_solution_summary: Detect pattern, annotate tenant as 'upgrade-quarantined', snapshot minimal state, exclude from upgrade waves, attempt guarded repair, resume or mark for manual escalation
rollback_plan: If new operator causes regressions, rollback operator to previous stable binary via staged helm release and clear quarantine annotation on affected tenants manually.
Manual checklist: take snapshot of tenant namespace, copy quarantine-metadata, remove annotation, run helm rollback to previous release id as last resort.
notes: Keep change small and observable. Prioritize safe defaults (detection-only) for initial rollout. Ensure clear customer-facing messaging to avoid surprises.
